outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the only development that bears directly on the conjecture is a preprint first posted in August 2023 (Pardon, arXiv:2308.02948, revised February 2024 and August 2025), which proves the Gromov–Witten / Donaldson–Pandharipande–Thomas equivalence for primary insertions on complex threefolds with nef anticanonical bundle (this includes every compact Calabi–Yau threefold). The descendent form and non-nef threefolds are outside that result as far as the sources I could read show. No journal publication, published error or expert write-up of Pardon's argument was found, and the other events in the window are refinements, toric, log or orbifold analogues, local-curve results, or expository.
problem_asks: The statement, as frozen, names one thing: an equivalence between Gromov–Witten (GW) theory and Donaldson–Thomas (DT) theory (the MNOP conjecture). Unpacked from the statement alone: (1) the GW side: generating series of GW invariants of 3-folds over all curve classes and all genera (genus variable u); (2) the DT side: generating series of DT invariants (counts of ideal sheaves, Euler characteristic variable q) over all curve classes and Euler characteristics; (3) the assertion that the two series agree after the substitution -q = e^{iu}, which the bullet does not write down and which comes from the literature; (4) the class of 3-folds: the bullet names none. The literature's MNOP covers compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds and general (projective) 3-folds, and I have taken the bullet to mean the conjecture in that full form; (5) insertions: the bullet does not say primary or descendent; the literature's MNOP covers both; (6) the DT side is the ideal-sheaf theory as named, while the proofs often state the stable-pair (PT) form, related to DT by a separate comparison. Read as a whole the bullet asks for the equivalence for all 3-folds with all insertions. Splitting it into the parts the literature treats separately (Calabi–Yau versus general, primary versus descendent, DT versus PT) is a map of the sub-cases, not a narrowing of the bullet.

events.what_happened: John Pardon, 'Universally counting curves in Calabi–Yau threefolds', arXiv:2308.02948 (math.AG). Per the arXiv abstract page: curve enumeration invariants of complex threefolds with nef anticanonical bundle are determined by their values on local curves; the abstract says this 'implies the MNOP conjecture of Maulik, Nekrasov, Okounkov, and Pandharipande' relating Gromov–Witten and Donaldson–Pandharipande–Thomas invariants, and that it 'hence holds for all complex threefolds with nef anti-canonical bundle (in particular, all Calabi-Yau threefolds)'. The local-curve case is cited as known from Bryan–Pandharipande and Okounkov–Pandharipande. The method is a Grothendieck group of 1-cycles together with a generic transversality result for holomorphic curves, following Ionel–Parker's proof of the Gopakumar–Vafa integrality conjecture. The v3 abstract-page paraphrase says 'with primary insertions'; that phrase is not in the verbatim segments I read, so it rests on that paraphrase plus the descriptions in the Lin–Wang and Pandharipande entries below. Quanta reports that in summer 2023 Pardon 'shared a proof online'.
events.revisions: v1 5 Aug 2023 (41 KB); v2 14 Feb 2024 (51 KB); v3 26 Aug 2025 (68 KB, current). What changed between versions was not established: I could not read the PDF text. The comments field gives '40 pages' in one fetch and '65 pages' in another.
events.delivers: For complex threefolds with nef anticanonical bundle (which includes every compact Calabi–Yau threefold): the MNOP equivalence between the GW and Donaldson–Pandharipande–Thomas generating series, for primary insertions. Restrictions carried: the nef anticanonical hypothesis; primary insertions only; the invariants are the Donaldson–Pandharipande–Thomas form named in the abstract, so the ideal-sheaf DT form of the bullet is reached only through a DT/PT comparison that I did not verify in Pardon's text.
events.remains: Descendent insertions (MNOP's descendent form). Threefolds whose anticanonical bundle is not nef, so general projective 3-folds outside that class. Per Lin–Wang's v2 comment, their own GW/PT descendent results 'are not covered by' Pardon's theorem, which is read as confirming the descendent part is not covered.

He builds on Pardon's theory and treats the MNOP proof as established; this is not an independent check of Pardon's argument.

events.time_since_posted: 3 years 2 months from v1 (5 Aug 2023) to 13 Oct 2026; no journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.doubts: No published error, gap, correction or retraction was found: a dedicated search for gap, error or doubt returned none. Points for the judging pass: (a) the abstract's restriction to nef anticanonical threefolds with primary insertions is narrower than several descriptions of the result. Wikipedia's 'John Pardon' article (opened) says he 'proved the MNOP conjecture ... of Calabi–Yau threefolds' with no restriction. Quanta (opened) says he 'proved a 20-year-old conjecture about counting curves' and gives no restriction. Behrend's introduction says Pardon 'proved the MNOP conjecture'. (b) The arXiv page reports no journal reference after three years, and I found no referee report, expert verification or blog working through the argument. (c) I could not read the PDF text, so a search summary's sentence that removing the nef hypothesis 'would be of exceptional interest' is unverified and I have not relied on it.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: it asserts that the GW and DPT generating series of complex threefolds with nef anticanonical bundle (so, all Calabi–Yau threefolds) agree under the MNOP change of variables, for primary insertions. It proves the conjecture in that class rather than refuting it.

events.what_happened: Yinbang Lin and Sz-Sheng Wang, 'Gromov–Witten/Pandharipande–Thomas correspondence via conifold transitions', arXiv:2310.18170. For a projective conifold transition from a smooth projective 3-fold X to Y, the abstract says that if the GW/PT descendent correspondence holds for the resolution Y, it also holds for the smoothing X with stationary descendent insertions, which yields the correspondence in new cases. Its v2 comment (April 2024) adds the reference to Pardon's work and says their results are not covered by his.
events.revisions: v1 27 Oct 2023; v2 17 Apr 2024 (adds the Pardon reference); v3 23 Jul 2025.
events.delivers: Conditional on the GW/PT descendent correspondence for a resolution Y, the same correspondence for the smoothing X with stationary descendent insertions. PT form, not DT. Conditional, stationary insertions only.
events.remains: The unconditional GW/PT descendent correspondence for Calabi–Yau 3-folds; non-stationary descendents; the DT (ideal-sheaf) form.
events.time_since_posted: 2 years 11 months from v1 to 13 Oct 2026
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: it transfers a GW/PT descendent identity from a resolution to a smoothing, conditional on the identity holding for the resolution.

events.what_happened: Rahul Pandharipande, 'Moduli of curves and moduli of sheaves', arXiv:2501.15607 (January 2025), an expository survey accompanying a lecture at ICBS in July 2024. It describes the GW/DT correspondence as 'proposed more than 20 years ago'. It states that the descendent and relative correspondences developed with A. Pixton 'led to the proof of the correspondence for the Calabi-Yau quintic 3-fold', credits Pardon's primary GW/P results (Theorem 4, families with Fano or Calabi–Yau 3-fold fibres, and a new proof of its Theorem 2), and says the 'full conjectural framework' is for families of 3-folds.
events.revisions: v1 only (26 Jan 2025).
events.delivers: No new theorem is claimed. As a survey it reports: the quintic proof (with Pixton, via descendent and relative correspondences for stable pairs); Pardon's primary GW/P result for families of Fano or Calabi–Yau fibres; and a conjectural framework for families of 3-folds. Its footnote 9, as read in the HTML fetch, says that 'for a fixed Calabi-Yau 3-fold X, the descendent and primary correspondence is equivalent'. If that statement carries Pardon's primary result over to descendents for Calabi–Yau 3-folds, the descendent gap is closed for those; I could not check the footnote against its full text, and Lin–Wang's comment points the other way.
events.remains: The general GW/DT correspondence for 3-folds, which the survey calls 'proposed'; the descendent correspondence for general 3-folds; the families framework, which is conjectural. Footnote 9 may or may not close the Calabi–Yau descendent part (see delivers).

checked_by.qualification: Co-author of the MNOP papers and of the Pandharipande–Pixton quintic work
checked_by.what_they_did: Describes Pardon's results and credits them with a new proof of one of the survey's theorems. This is credit and use, not an independent check.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: it reports the quintic case and Pardon's primary case as established, and the general case as proposed.

events.what_happened: Kai Behrend, 'A Pardon Algebra for Zero-cycles', arXiv:2604.05534 (7 April 2026). Builds an analogue of Pardon's 1-cycle construction for 0-cycles on d-folds, presented as a simplified version of Pardon's theory. The abstract says that 'Recently, John Pardon proved the MNOP conjecture' and that the construction gives a new point of view on point-counting enumerative problems, including the degree-zero MNOP conjecture for Hilbert schemes of points on projective 3-folds. The abstract does not claim to prove that degree-zero case.
events.revisions: v1 only (7 Apr 2026).
events.delivers: A zero-cycle version of Pardon's construction and its relation to point-counting enumerative problems. It does not establish a new case of the GW/DT equivalence for 3-folds in what I read. It is about 0-cycles on curves and d-folds, not the 1-cycle theory used for the 3-fold result.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks for 3-folds is left to Pardon's theory; this paper does not address it.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; it takes Pardon's MNOP proof as given and builds on it.

events.what_happened: Davesh Maulik and Dhruv Ranganathan, 'The GW/PT conjectures for toric pairs', arXiv:2603.07772 (8 March 2026; v2 13 April 2026). Proves the logarithmic GW/PT correspondence for pairs (Y | ∂Y) with Y a toric threefold and ∂Y any torus-invariant divisor, with primary insertions. Also covers a 2008 conjecture on the capped vertex (per the abstract page, which does not name its authors here), and verifies the logarithmic DT/PT conjecture for toric threefold pairs. v2 comments say results were 'strengthened to remove dependence on prior work'.
events.revisions: v1 8 Mar 2026; v2 13 Apr 2026 (results strengthened to remove dependence on prior work, per the comments field).
events.delivers: The GW/PT correspondence for toric threefold pairs (log, with ∂Y any torus-invariant divisor), primary insertions only, per the abstract page. A search snippet of a talk listing said 'primary and descendent'; the abstract page I read says primary.
events.remains: Compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds (no boundary divisor) are not the setting; non-toric threefolds; descendent insertions (not claimed in the abstract I read).
events.direction: Consistent with the GW/PT form of the conjecture in a log, toric setting. An analogue of MNOP, not the compact Calabi–Yau statement.

events.what_happened: A seminar listing, 'AI-assisted proofs in Mirror Symmetry' (Michel van Garrel, University of Birmingham; KAIST, 2 July 2026), describes an ongoing joint project with Siebert. The authors aim to show that the generating function of Gromov–Witten invariants of a Calabi–Yau variety equals the expansion of a canonical period integral on its intrinsic mirror. The listing says the project 'heavily relies on AI-assisted proofs', without naming any AI system. I found no preprint or write-up.
events.revisions: None found. The date is the talk date from the listing; no written argument was found, so the first public written argument is undated.
events.delivers: Not established: an announced ongoing project on GW generating functions versus intrinsic mirror periods, which is about Gromov–Witten invariants, not the GW/DT equivalence.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; the project is not an equivalence between GW and DT theory.
events.direction: Not a claim about the conjecture. Recorded because it is an AI-involved Gromov–Witten project in the same area.

events.what_happened: Johannes Schmitt, 'Extremal descendant integrals on moduli spaces of curves: An inequality discovered and proved in collaboration with AI', arXiv:2512.14575 (16 December 2025). An inequality for pure psi-class intersection numbers on the moduli space of curves: the value is minimal for powers of a single class and maximal for balanced vectors, proved using nefness and Khovanskii–Teissier log-concavity.
events.revisions: Only the v1 date was read.
events.delivers: An inequality for psi-class intersection numbers on the moduli space of curves. This is a different problem from the GW/DT equivalence. It is recorded because it is an AI-involved paper in the Gromov–Witten neighbourhood.
events.remains: Not applicable: a different question.

events.what_happened: R. Pandharipande and A. Pixton, 'Gromov–Witten/Pairs correspondence for the quintic 3-fold', arXiv:1206.5490 (24 June 2012). Uses the GW/Pairs descendent correspondence for toric 3-folds, with degeneration arguments and a study of descendents in relative geometries, to establish the GW/Pairs correspondence for several compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds, including all Calabi–Yau complete intersections in products of projective spaces (the quintic is in that class). After change of variables the GW series is a rational function in −q = e^{iu} invariant under q ↔ 1/q. Published J. Amer. Math. Soc. 30 (2017), per the AMS URL seen in search results.
events.revisions: v1 24 Jun 2012; v2 23 Jan 2016 ('revised version'); JAMS 2017 per search-listed URL.
events.delivers: GW/Pairs (stable-pair, PT form) correspondence for several compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds including the quintic, and the rationality and q ↔ 1/q symmetry of the GW side for those. Restrictions: PT form; the Calabi–Yau complete intersections in products of projective spaces. The abstract does not say whether the result covers primary insertions only or descendents as well. Pandharipande's 2025 survey states that for a fixed Calabi–Yau 3-fold the descendent and primary correspondences are equivalent (see the survey event), which if right makes the scope matter less; I did not verify this.
events.remains: Other compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds; the DT (ideal-sheaf) form, which needs a DT/PT comparison; general 3-folds.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: it establishes the GW/PT form for the quintic and similar Calabi–Yau complete intersections.

events.what_happened: R. Pandharipande and A. Pixton, 'Gromov–Witten/Pairs descendent correspondence for toric 3-folds', arXiv:1203.0468 (2 March 2012). Constructs a fully equivariant correspondence between GW and stable-pairs descendent theories for toric 3-folds, shows it has a non-equivariant limit, and proves an explicit non-equivariant stationary descendent correspondence for toric X, which the abstract says was conjectured by MNOP. Also gives relative GW/Pairs correspondences in several log Calabi–Yau geometries and a rationality constraint for P^3.
events.revisions: v1 2 Mar 2012; later versions not read.
events.delivers: Toric 3-folds: the equivariant GW/Pairs descendent correspondence, its non-equivariant limit, and the stationary non-equivariant descendent correspondence (conjectured by MNOP). PT form. Toric only.
events.remains: Non-toric 3-folds; compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds with non-stationary descendents; the DT form.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the toric descendent case.

events.what_happened: A. Oblomkov, A. Okounkov and R. Pandharipande, 'GW/PT descendent correspondence via vertex operators', arXiv:1806.00714 (2 June 2018). Proposes an explicit formula for the GW/PT descendent correspondence in the stationary case for nonsingular projective 3-folds, written with vertex operators, and proves it for all nonsingular projective toric 3-folds. Published Commun. Math. Phys. 374 (2020), per the search snippet.
events.revisions: v1 2 Jun 2018; a v3 is listed in search results; later versions not read.
events.delivers: Stationary GW/PT descendent correspondence: proposed for all nonsingular projective 3-folds, proved for nonsingular projective toric 3-folds only. PT form.
events.remains: The stationary proposal for non-toric 3-folds; non-stationary descendents; the DT form; compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; its general case is a proposal, its toric case a theorem.

events.what_happened: D. Maulik, A. Oblomkov, A. Okounkov and R. Pandharipande, 'Gromov–Witten/Donaldson–Thomas correspondence for toric 3-folds', arXiv:0809.3976 (23 September 2008). Proves that the equivariant GW theory of a nonsingular toric 3-fold with primary insertions is equivalent to its equivariant DT theory. Corollary: the topological vertex calculations of Aganagic, Klemm, Mariño and Vafa for local Calabi–Yau toric 3-folds are correct in the full three-leg setting.
events.revisions: v1 23 Sep 2008; later versions not read.
events.delivers: Nonsingular toric 3-folds, equivariant, primary insertions, DT (ideal-sheaf) form. Consistent with the bullet's DT form, restricted to toric geometry.
events.remains: Non-toric 3-folds; non-equivariant statement (not read); descendent insertions; compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the toric case.

events.what_happened: Dustin Ross, 'On GW/DT and Ruan's Conjecture in All Genus for Calabi-Yau 3-Orbifolds', arXiv:1409.7015 (24 September 2014). For toric Calabi–Yau 3-orbifolds with transverse A-singularities, proves Ruan's crepant resolution conjecture and the GW/DT correspondence. The 'all genus' phrase is in the title; the abstract I read does not mention genus. Published Comm. Math. Phys. (2015) per a Springer link seen in search results (not opened).
events.revisions: v1 24 Sep 2014; later versions not read.
events.delivers: GW/DT correspondence for toric Calabi–Yau 3-orbifolds with transverse A-singularities (per the abstract), with the all-genus claim as the title states. Orbifold analogue: not smooth Calabi–Yau 3-folds.
events.remains: Smooth compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds; non-toric orbifolds; descendent insertions.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the orbifold toric case. Discounted as an analogue (orbifolds).

events.what_happened: J. Bryan and R. Pandharipande, 'The local Gromov–Witten theory of curves', arXiv:math/0411037 (2 November 2004). Solves the local GW theory of curves by localization on P^1 and a TQFT built by degeneration for higher genus. Its abstract says the local GW theory of curves is equivalent to the local DT theory of curves and to the quantum cohomology of the Hilbert scheme of points of C^2 and the orbifold quantum cohomology of the symmetric product.
events.revisions: v1 2 Nov 2004; later versions not read.
events.delivers: The GW side of the local-curve case of the MNOP equivalence (local geometries over curves). Restricted to local curves, not compact 3-folds.
events.remains: Compact 3-folds; all cases outside local curves.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the local-curve case.

events.what_happened: A. Okounkov and R. Pandharipande, 'The local Donaldson–Thomas theory of curves', arXiv:math/0512573 (26 December 2005). Solves the local DT theory of curves by localization and degeneration. Completes a triangle of equivalences between GW theory of local curves, DT theory of local curves and quantum cohomology of the Hilbert scheme of points of the plane. Published Geom. Topol. 14 (2010), per a search snippet.
events.revisions: v1 26 Dec 2005; later versions not read.
events.delivers: The DT side of the local-curve case: equivalence with local GW of curves. Restricted to local curves.
events.remains: Compact 3-folds; everything outside local curves.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the local-curve case.

events.what_happened: K. Behrend and B. Fantechi, 'Symmetric obstruction theories and Hilbert schemes of points on threefolds', arXiv:math/0512556 (24 December 2005). Computes the zero-dimensional DT invariants of any projective Calabi–Yau 3-fold, and states that this proves a conjecture of MNOP. The abstract as I read it (paraphrased by the fetch tool) says 'Moreover, we calculate the zero-dimensional Donaldson-Thomas invariants of any projective Calabi-Yau 3-fold'.
events.revisions: v1 24 Dec 2005; later versions not read.
events.delivers: Degree-zero (zero-dimensional DT invariant) part of the MNOP equivalence, for projective Calabi–Yau 3-folds. Restricted to degree zero.
events.remains: Positive-degree (curve-class) invariants; descendent insertions; the GW side of the degree-zero comparison as stated in the MNOP paper (not read).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in degree zero.

events.what_happened: Jun Li, 'Zero dimensional Donaldson–Thomas invariants of threefolds', arXiv:math/0604490 (23 April 2006). Proves 'a conjecture' of MNOP for zero-dimensional DT invariants, by a homotopy approach. Per a search snippet (not read in full), the main theorem covers all compact smooth complex 3-folds and gives the MacMahon-function formula. Published Geom. Topol. 10(4) (2006), per the search snippet.
events.revisions: v1 23 Apr 2006; later versions not read.
events.delivers: Degree-zero (zero-dimensional DT invariant) part of MNOP, per the abstract. Scope to all compact smooth 3-folds comes from a search snippet, not from the text I read.

events.what_happened: Tom Bridgeland, 'Hall algebras and curve-counting invariants', arXiv:1002.4374 (23 February 2010). Uses Joyce's motivic Hall algebras to prove that reduced DT curve-counting invariants on Calabi–Yau threefolds coincide with stable-pair invariants, and that their generating functions are Laurent expansions of rational functions.
events.revisions: v1 23 Feb 2010; later versions not read.
events.delivers: Reduced DT and stable-pair invariants of Calabi–Yau 3-folds coincide, with rationality. This is the DT/PT comparison that links the PT-form results (Pardon's, Pandharipande–Pixton's) to the DT form of the bullet. Restricted to reduced invariants on Calabi–Yau 3-folds.
events.remains: The non-reduced (unweighted) DT invariants, which search snippets attribute to Toda (not read); general 3-folds; the GW side.
events.direction: Consistent with the DT form of the conjecture; it is the comparison step, not a GW result.

events.what_happened: Denis Nesterov, 'Quasimaps to moduli spaces of sheaves', arXiv:2111.11417 (22 November 2021). Develops quasimaps to a moduli space of sheaves M on a surface S. Via Zhou's entangled tails, a wall-crossing formula relates the GW theory of M to the DT theory of S×C with relative insertions, where C is a nodal curve. Evaluated for Hilbert schemes of points when S is a del Pezzo surface. Published in Forum of Mathematics, Pi (2025), per a DOAJ search snippet (not opened).
events.revisions: v1 22 Nov 2021; published Forum Math. Pi 2025 per search snippet.
events.delivers: A wall-crossing between GW of moduli of sheaves on a surface and DT of S×C. S×C are threefolds that are not in general Calabi–Yau. A quasimap analogue of GW/DT.
events.remains: The MNOP equivalence for Calabi–Yau 3-folds and general 3-folds as stated.
events.direction: Analogue: a related GW/DT wall-crossing on different threefolds. Discounted for this bullet.

events.what_happened: Andrea Brini and Yannik Schuler, 'Refined Gromov–Witten invariants', arXiv:2410.00118 (v1 30 September 2024). Conjectures that the disconnected equivariant GW generating series of X × C² returns the Nekrasov–Okounkov K-theoretic PT partition function (a refined GW/PT correspondence for Calabi–Yau threefolds with a C* action). Proves it for the resolved conifold, proves a refined cycle-level local/relative correspondence for local del Pezzo surfaces, and proves extended holomorphic anomaly equations.
events.revisions: v1 30 Sep 2024; later versions not read.
events.delivers: A conjectured refinement, with proofs only in the resolved conifold and local del Pezzo cases. Refined (K-theoretic) and conjectural in general.
events.remains: The refined correspondence for general Calabi–Yau 3-folds; the unrefined MNOP equivalence is not addressed.
events.direction: Refinement: consistent with the physics expectations; a different question from the unrefined bullet.

events.what_happened: Sergej Monavari, 'The refined local Donaldson–Thomas theory of curves', arXiv:2506.14359 (17 June 2025). Solves the K-theoretically refined DT theory of local curves in arbitrary genus and degree by localisation, and derives the K-theoretic DT/PT correspondence for local curves (as conjectured by Nekrasov–Okounkov). Says that, thanks to Pardon's machinery, the local-curve results are expected to play a key role toward the refined GW/PT correspondence of Brini–Schuler for all smooth Calabi–Yau threefolds. That is an expectation, not a claim.
events.revisions: v1 17 Jun 2025; later versions not read.
events.delivers: Refined DT and PT theory of local curves; the K-theoretic DT/PT correspondence for local curves. Local curves only, refined.
events.remains: Compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds; the unrefined MNOP equivalence; the refined GW/PT conjecture.
events.direction: Analogue and refinement on local curves. Discounted for this bullet.

events.what_happened: Chih-Huan Chang, 'Motivic DT/PT Correspondence', arXiv:2511.22213 (27 November 2025). Proves a motivic version of the DT/PT correspondence on Calabi–Yau threefolds, using Toda's wall-crossing framework and a motivic integral identity of Bu. Gives a refinement of the numerical DT/PT correspondence. Not a Gromov–Witten statement.
events.revisions: v1 27 Nov 2025; later versions not read.
events.delivers: A motivic refinement of DT/PT on Calabi–Yau 3-folds. Concerns the DT–PT comparison, not the GW side.
events.remains: The GW side of the equivalence; the unrefined MNOP statement as such.
events.direction: Refinement of the DT–PT comparison step. Discounted as a different question (motivic, DT/PT only).

events.what_happened: Reginald Anderson, 'Examples of descendent generating series for Pandharipande–Thomas stable pairs on smooth projective Fano threefolds via one-dimensional wall-crossing', arXiv:2607.02526. Computes examples of one-dimensional DT invariants and PT descendent generating series on Fano 3-folds (P^3, a cubic threefold, blow-ups of P^3, a projective bundle over P^1×P^1), and compares them with formulas of Pandharipande and Moreira. Not a GW/DT equivalence statement.
events.revisions: The page reports v1 11 May 2026 and v2 10 Sep 2026. The identifier 2607 suggests July 2026, which conflicts with the reported date; unresolved.

disputes.summary: Descriptions of the result differ on scope. Pardon's abstract restricts the proof to complex threefolds with nef anticanonical bundle and (per the v3 abstract-page paraphrase) primary insertions. Wikipedia's 'John Pardon' article (opened) says he proved 'the MNOP conjecture ... of Calabi–Yau threefolds' with no restriction. Quanta (opened) says he 'proved a 20-year-old conjecture' with no restriction. Behrend's introduction says 'Pardon used his theory to prove the MNOP Gromov-Witten-Donaldson-Thomas correspondence'. Wikipedia's 'Donaldson–Thomas theory' article (opened, revision of 20 Sep 2026) says MNOP proved GW and DT equivalence 'in increasing generality'. The record reports the abstract's scope and leaves the weighing to the judging pass.

A search snippet (TechTimes, not opened) says Pardon's 2026 Fields Medal citation credits 'the proof of the MNOP conjecture'. The IMU page (opened) and the Stony Brook SCGP page (opened) give the citation as 'achievements in symplectic geometry, including new approaches to virtual fundamental cycles', 'Fukaya categories ... and counting holomorphic curves', and 'contributions to other areas of geometry and topology, including group actions on 3-manifolds and knot theory', and do not name MNOP, Gromov–Witten, Donaldson–Thomas or Calabi–Yau. The TechTimes gloss is not supported by the primary sources I read. The medal is an honour, not a verification, and is not recorded as an event.

summary: The main finding is a single preprint that predates the frozen revision. Pardon, arXiv:2308.02948, first posted 5 August 2023 and revised 14 February 2024 and 26 August 2025, proves the MNOP equivalence (Gromov–Witten versus the Donaldson–Pandharipande–Thomas form) for complex threefolds with nef anticanonical bundle, which includes every compact Calabi–Yau threefold, for primary insertions. The method shows the invariants are determined by their values on local curves, where the case was already known from Bryan–Pandharipande and Okounkov–Pandharipande. I could not read the PDF (the arXiv PDF and the Stony Brook copy both returned unreadable binary), so the scope comes from the arXiv abstract page (read in several fetches, with the verbatim segments consistent with each other), from Lin–Wang's v2 comment that their GW/PT results are 'not covered by his' and that his theorem is without descendents, and from Pandharipande's January 2025 survey, which credits Pardon's Theorem 4 for primary GW/P in families with Fano or Calabi–Yau fibres. Descendent insertions and non-nef threefolds are outside the result on those readings. Two things cut the other way and are not resolved here. The survey's footnote 9 (read through the HTML fetch) says that for a fixed Calabi–Yau 3-fold the descendent and primary correspondences are equivalent, which if right would carry Pardon's result to descendents for those; I could not verify the footnote's wording against the paper. Pandharipande–Pixton (2012, JAMS 2017) also proves a GW/Pairs case for the quintic and similar complete intersections, and the survey says the descendent and primary correspondences are equivalent for a fixed Calabi–Yau 3-fold; so the scope question is live. Status-wise: no journal reference appears on the arXiv page after three years; a search for gaps, errors or doubts returned none; no referee report or expert write-up of Pardon's argument was found; and the only public engagement is by people building on it (Lin–Wang's scope note, Pandharipande's survey credit, and Behrend's April 2026 zero-cycle paper, which calls the curve case 'an exploration of John Pardon's theory' and says Pardon 'proved the MNOP conjecture'). Journalistic and reference descriptions (Quanta, Wikipedia's Pardon article, the Wikipedia Donaldson–Thomas article) describe the MNOP conjecture as proved without the nef or primary restriction; the list entry's link now redirects to 'Donaldson–Thomas theory'. Pardon won the 2026 Fields Medal, but the IMU citation does not name MNOP, and I have treated the medal as an honour, not an event. The older events that the status rests on in part are: Bryan–Pandharipande (2004) and Okounkov–Pandharipande (2005) for local curves; Behrend–Fantechi (2005) and Li (2006) for degree zero, the Calabi–Yau and general projective cases respectively; Maulik–Oblomkov–Okounkov–Pandharipande (2008) for toric primary insertions; Pandharipande–Pixton (2012) for the toric descendent correspondence and for the quintic; Bridgeland (2010) for the reduced DT/PT comparison; Oblomkov–Okounkov–Pandharipande (2018) for a stationary descendent proposal proved for toric 3-folds; and Ross (2014) for toric Calabi–Yau orbifolds. Analogues and refinements in the window (Brini–Schuler, Maulik–Ranganathan, Monavari, Chang) are recorded and discounted. On AI: I found no AI system involved in the MNOP equivalence or in any event on it. My searches covered the problem's names, proof-related wording, AI terms, lab announcements, Lean/Mathlib, and open-problem trackers. The nearest AI-involved items are recorded as discarded events: Schmitt (December 2025), a different problem on psi-class inequalities, where the authors credit GPT-5, Gemini 3 Pro and Claude Opus 4.5; van Garrel–Siebert (July 2026), an announced project on Gromov–Witten generating functions and intrinsic mirror periods, described as relying on unnamed 'AI-assisted proofs', with no write-up; and Anderson (2607.02526), with an unnamed 'AI acknowledgements' comment on a PT paper. OpenAI's August 2026 Astra list of ten problems, as reported in coverage I did not open in full, contains no Gromov–Witten or Donaldson–Thomas item, and Epoch's FrontierMath open-problems page has none either. The calls I made: (1) I read the bullet as the full MNOP statement, 3-folds in general with primary and descendent insertions, Calabi–Yau being the central case; (2) I recorded the 2023 Pardon preprint as the first public written argument, before the frozen revision, so the 'since January 2024' status is carried by its later versions and the absence of other events; (3) I treated the Fields Medal as not an event and the TechTimes gloss as unsupported.
competing_reading: Read the bullet as the MNOP equivalence in the form the community uses for 'the MNOP conjecture', where the central case is Calabi–Yau threefolds. On that reading Pardon's theorem covers every compact Calabi–Yau threefold for primary insertions, the local and toric cases were already known, and the problem is substantially settled since 2023 by a preprint that has not appeared in a journal. The sources that say so include Quanta, Wikipedia's Pardon article and Behrend's introduction. The opposite reading: the bullet names no class and does not restrict insertions, so the conjecture as MNOP stated it also covers descendent insertions and general 3-folds. On that reading Pardon's theorem settles one part, primary insertions on nef anticanonical threefolds, and the rest stays open unless the survey's footnote 9 carries the primary result to descendents for Calabi–Yau 3-folds. Lin–Wang's comment supports the opposite reading on descendents.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of Pardon's theorem and corollary in arXiv:2308.02948 (v1 and v3): the hypotheses, the insertion type, whether the DT form is stated or only the DPT form, and what changed between versions. The PDF was not readable through the tools here, so this is the first thing to get. (2) A journal reference for arXiv:2308.02948, or a referee or expert report. (3) Whether Pandharipande's footnote 9 (arXiv:2501.15607, descendent and primary correspondences equivalent for a fixed Calabi–Yau 3-fold) means that Pardon's primary result gives descendents for Calabi–Yau 3-folds; this needs the survey's own text. (4) The full text of Pandharipande–Pixton (arXiv:1206.5490) to settle whether the quintic result covers descendents. (5) The MNOP papers' own list of conjectures (math/0312059 and math/0406092), to fix whether 'the conjecture' includes general 3-folds and descendents, which decides whether the Calabi–Yau primary result is the whole bullet. (6) A check that Lin–Wang's v2 scope note and the 2026 Behrend paper's 'proved' wording refer to the same theorem.

judgement.why: The statement names the MNOP equivalence without restricting the class of 3-folds or the insertions, so Pardon's theorem (nef anticanonical 3-folds, primary insertions, DPT form) is a case, not the whole; it is dated to its August 2023 v1 because nothing shows the 2024/2025 revisions add new mathematics, so it falls before the snapshot. Its engagement (Pandharipande crediting and using it, Behrend building on it, Lin–Wang scoping against it) is uptake rather than a worked check, so it stays unreviewed, but nothing gives reason for doubt. Post-snapshot items are a survey and a building-on paper (none), log/refined/motivic/orbifold analogues (variant), an announcement and a psi-class inequality on a different problem (variant; Schmitt's AI credit is genuine generation but for a different question), and a PT-only computation (none). Pre-snapshot local-curve, degree-zero, toric and quintic results are cases; only those with a journal of record in the record are marked digested; Bridgeland's DT/PT comparison has no GW content and is none.
judgement.doubts: Close call on Pardon's scope: if the bullet is read as only the Calabi–Yau primary MNOP conjecture, Pardon would be whole — but it is pre-snapshot either way, so the problem's post-snapshot status is unaffected. Pandharipande's footnote 9 (primary and descendent equivalent for a fixed CY 3-fold) is unverified. Several pre-snapshot papers are published per snippets but the record logs no checked_by, so they are left unreviewed.
